subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Café de Flore: Art and Revolution
description: A micro-lesson that makes Café de Flore: Art and Revolution usable.

hook.text: Café de Flore sits just meters from Les Deux Magots. The two cafés competed fiercely for intellectual talent.

buildup.text: Picasso, Camus, Apollinaire, and the surrealists all frequented Café de Flore during the early 20th century.

discovery.text: During the Nazi occupation, Flore became a quiet haven. Resistance writers gathered discreetly between its red banquettes.

twist.text: After liberation, it became a celebrity haunt. Fashion designers and film stars replaced philosophers at the zinc bar.

climax.text: Today, a single espresso at Flore costs several euros—but you're renting a seat at one of art history's great stages.

punchline.text: From resistance to runway culture, all at the same small tables.

quiz.question: What role did Café de Flore play during World War II?
options: It served as a quiet meeting place for resistance writers
It became a German officers' club

details.summary: Cafe de Flore on Paris's Boulevard Saint-Germain has been a hub for artists and intellectuals since the 1880s. Picasso, Sartre, and de Beauvoir held court there. During the Occupation, its warmth attracted writers who could not heat their apartments.
details.whyItMatters: Cafe de Flore represents the French tradition of the cafe as a stage for artistic and philosophical movements. Its history mirrors a century of French culture.
takeaways: Cafe de Flore has operated since the 1880s on Boulevard Saint-Germain
Sartre, de Beauvoir, and Picasso were famous regulars
It became a wartime refuge for writers during the Occupation

faq.question: Why did Sartre and de Beauvoir work at Cafe de Flore?
faq.answer: During the German occupation of Paris, fuel was scarce and apartments were freezing. Cafe de Flore had a coal stove, warmth, and light. Sartre and de Beauvoir wrote there daily for years, making it the de facto headquarters of existentialism.

faq.question: Can you still visit Cafe de Flore today?
faq.answer: Yes. It operates at 172 Boulevard Saint-Germain and retains its art deco interior. Prices are high and it is touristy, but its atmosphere remains distinctive. It still attracts writers and artists alongside visitors drawn by its legendary reputation.
